stem: Albinism is a condition that results from disruption of a biosynthetic pathway involving the enzyme tyrosinase. It is estimated that 1 in 17 000 people in the world has albinism.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
A recessive mutation in the $TYR$ gene, which codes for the enzyme tyrosinase, is one cause of albinism. Individuals with this form of albinism are homozygous recessive.

Describe the phenotype of a person with albinism.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem:
A recessive mutation in a different gene causes a type of albinism that mainly affects the eyes (ocular albinism). A person with this condition has reduced clarity of vision and involuntary eye movements.

Fig. 2.1 shows the pattern of inheritance of ocular albinism in one family. The pattern indicates sex-linked inheritance.

{{figure:figure_2_1.png}}

Key: ○ = unaffected female
⊙ = carrier female
□ = unaffected male
■ = male with ocular albinism

Fig. 2.1

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Explain why Fig. 2.1 supports sex-linked inheritance of ocular albinism.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
Ocular albinism may be caused by a base deletion mutation. This mutation results in a non-functional protein.

Explain how a base deletion mutation can result in a non-functional protein.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text:
Ocular albinism is a non-progressive disorder and clarity of vision remains stable throughout life.

A female has a family history of ocular albinism but she does not have any symptoms. A test to find out if she has the mutant allele is available.

Suggest **one** reason for taking this test and **one** reason against taking this test.
